title: Windows and Edge distrust eMudhra CAs after private keys were exposed
summary: Private keys for eight eMudhra G3B/G3C intermediate CAs (six TLS, two code signing) were recoverable, so anyone holding them could mint trusted-looking certificates or sign code. On 20 October 2026 Microsoft blocked the eight keys by SPKI in the Windows Disallowed Certificate Trust List and in the Edge/WebView2 CRLSet. On 26 October an out-of-band Windows update removed six eMudhra G3 roots and an AAA Certificate Services cross-sign from the Windows trust list, and Edge followed on 27 October. Update (MC1529467, 11 November): on 16 November 2026 an Edge/WebView2 PKI Metadata component update removes default trust for the remaining roots — emSign Root CA - G1, emSign Root CA - C1, emSign ECC Root CA and emSign Root TLS CA - G1 — and devices check for it every 10 hours and shortly after app launch.
why: Two things can bite you: internal or partner services with certificates chaining to the removed roots will start failing TLS, and disconnected or image-based machines that don't pull certificate trust list updates keep trusting certificates an attacker could forge, including signed malware.
todo: Check whether anything you run or depend on chains to eMudhra: scan internal TLS endpoints and code-signing chains against the certificate list in the Microsoft Trusted Root Program announcement, and replace those certificates now.

Before 16 November, test internal and partner sites and WebView2-based line-of-business apps whose certificates chain to an emSign root: after the PKI Metadata update they stop being trusted in Edge and WebView2.

Confirm automatic root and disallowed CTL updates reach clients and servers. For offline or proxied networks, distribute the updated CTLs as described in 'Configure trusted roots and disallowed certificates'.
Redeploy VM Scale Sets and single-instance VMs from the updated Azure Marketplace images if they are disconnected from Windows Update.
Do not re-add the removed roots locally to fix a broken app without a risk decision; software that doesn't check revocation or the disallowed list would then accept forged certificates.
effective_note: Disallowed CTL and Edge CRLSet block on 20 Oct; root removal 26 Oct (Windows) and 27 Oct (Edge); remaining emSign roots removed from Edge/WebView2 on 16 Nov 2026
